subject: Interim sovereignty guardrails & evidence onboarding
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@mediq.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@mediq.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Interim sovereignty guardrails and evidence onboarding

Tessa,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re in the final stage of our architecture review and need a short-term binding that our demo and initial production traffic will remain within our chosen geography (US) for customer data that is subject to state-level protections. The contract team suggested we get an "interim sovereignty" package while the DPA addendum is finalized.

What we need from Redwood in the next 5 business days:
- A compact evidence package (logs audit sample, subprocessor roster, KMS region mapping)
- Confirmation of temporary egress windows and exactly what triggers cross-region failover
- A short statement on encryption key residency and whether we can require US-only KMS keys for our environment

We are okay with a controlled exception policy as long as it is timeboxed, auditable, and includes notification hooks to our security team.

Can you confirm feasibility and proposed timeline? We’ll need to present to our CISO on 9/20.

Appreciate it,
Alex

Attachment: mediq_request_summary.pdf (stub)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@mediq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interim sovereignty guardrails and evidence onboarding

Alex — thanks for the clarity. We can assemble an interim package that covers the asks you listed. Quick outline / proposed next steps: 

1) Evidence pack (deliver by 2027-09-15):
   - Sample audit logs (anonymized) showing regional ingress/egress markers
   - Current subprocessor roster with activation dates and regions
   - KMS mapping for your tenant and a short description of key residency options

2) Temporary egress window policy (proposal attached):
   - Define triggers: (a) regional outage > X min; (b) capacity exhaustion on dedicated pool; (c) customer-approved incident
   - Timebox: default 72 hours; extension requires written approval from Mediq security
   - Notification: automated email + webhook to Legal Ops and Security distribution lists

3) Formal statement on US-only KMS requirement — we need to confirm with infra ops whether we can enforce tenant-level KMS restrictions in Private and Dedicated modes. If on Hosted we will offer a contractual commitment where keys are customer-managed and pinned to US-only HSM (where the customer supplies KMS).

Internal notes: Marissa, Ben — can you pull the anonymized audit sample and subprocessor roster? Kimberly — can you confirm KMS tenant pinning feasibility and any lead time for key escrow/rotation?

If we can hit the 9/15 deliverable, Alex, that should be sufficient for your team’s presentation on 9/20 as long as the timeline and transient-egress SLA language are visible.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (referenced) region-pin-matrix.csv (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@mediq.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interim sovereignty guardrails and evidence onboarding

Team — pulling the pieces together. A few operational clarifications for the evidence pack: 

- Audit logs: we’ll provide a 7-day anonymized extract showing the region attribute and the routing decision (local vs fallback). We will strip PII and sequence ids; sample will include timestamps and trace IDs for correlation.
- Subprocessor roster: includes current cloud infra partners, monitoring vendors, and any transient telemetry processors. We will flag any APAC/EU subprocessors and include activation windows.
- KMS: for Dedicated and Private we can require customer-managed keys in a US region; on Hosted we offer a managed-Key-to-Customer policy where we pin encryption material to US HSMs for an addendum. We need Legal to confirm whether that satisfies a contractual "US-only KMS" clause.

Question for Mediq: do you want the audit sample to show failed/fallback events? That will show transient egress and help quantify frequency, but it might require a short escalation to infra sec for approval.

Also attaching a compact ZIP with redacted extracts and a proposed egress-notice template. If Mediq wants, we can add an automated webhook payload example for notification.

--Marissa

Attachments: mediq-evidence-pack.zip (contains redacted-logs.txt, subprocessor-roster.csv, egress_notice_template.txt)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@mediq.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interim sovereignty guardrails and evidence onboarding

Alex — sending the assembled package and proposed acceptance criteria. High-level summary for Mediq’s CISO: 

1) What we’re delivering now (in mediq-evidence-pack.zip):
   - Redacted 7-day audit extract with region routing flags and anonymized trace IDs
   - Subprocessor roster with region tags and activation dates (CSV)
   - Proposed egress-notice template and webhook sample payload
   - Region pin matrix (region-pin-matrix.csv) showing modes (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and enforcement level

2) Operational acceptance criteria we propose:
   - Any cross-region processing event must be triggered only by documented outage criteria or explicit customer authorization
   - Default transient egress window = 72 hours; any extension requires written approval from Mediq security and is logged in our audit trail
   - Notification to Mediq security by email and webhook within 15 minutes of failover initiation
   - Proof: we will provide a post-incident audit record with trace IDs and timestamps within 48 hours of the event

3) KMS/customer keys: for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed US-resident keys. For Hosted we will offer an addendum that pins encryption keys to US HSMs (customer-managed preferred). Legal can provide contract language ASAP (DocuSign link included).

If this aligns with your expectation, we can: (a) add the short DPA addendum language; (b) sign a timeboxed exception addendum that will be superseded by the final DPA; (c) provide an ongoing telemetry webhook to Mediq for any routed requests.

Alex — let us know if you want a 30-minute call with Infra Ops and Legal tomorrow to walk through the package before the CISO meeting.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Forwarded-For: mediq-evidence-pack.zip, region-pin-matrix.csv (attached)
